newsitem.title: UK: Lead oversupply in 1997, zinc in shortfall - ILZSG.
newsitem.headline: Lead oversupply in 1997, zinc in shortfall - ILZSG.

text.p: World refined output of lead next year is estimated rising to 5.92 million tonnes, exceeding consumption of 5.86 million tonnes, the International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) said.
Meanwhile, global zinc consumption of 7.77 million tonnes will outpace mine production of 7.33 million tonnes, ILZSG said in a release received here following meetings in Vienna.

The ILZSG said world lead consumption will rise by 2.6 percent in 1997, reflecting increases in Europe and the Far East. However, refined output will rise by by 5.6 percent, largely due to increases in European output.
"In 1997, refined metal supply will exceed demand by a modest amount for the first time since 1994," ILZSG said.
Zinc consumption is expected to register a 2.8-percent increase, while supply will rise 3.9 percent, mostly due to extra production in Europe and the Far East.
But demand is still seen exceeding demand for the third successive year. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8080
